harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Restricted cron job scheduling on node1 (Alpine Linux, busybox crond) to only root and opsadmin. Since busybox's crontab does not support /etc/cron.allow /etc/cron.deny and its setuid helper (bbsuid) grants root escalation to any user invoking /usr/bin/crontab, I replaced /usr/bin/crontab with a wrapper script that checks the calling user against an allowlist (root, opsadmin) before delegating to the real bbsuid-backed crontab applet (relocated to /usr/lib/cron-helper/bbsuid-crontab, invoked with argv0=/usr/bin/crontab so bbsuid's hardcoded path dispatch still matches). Created the opsadmin user. Verified root and opsadmin can create/list/remove crontabs while other users (alpine, nobody) are denied with a clear error. Restarted node1 via native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed (3f62700c... -> 6c2ecdfb...), and re-verified after restart that the wrapper, opsadmin account, root's original system crontab (periodic run-parts jobs), and the access restriction all persisted and function correctly. Cleaned up all test crontab entries left over from verification.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Alpine Linux 3.23.3, busybox crond/crontab via setuid bbsuid helper with no cron.allow/cron.deny support
Confirmed baseline: bbsuid unconditionally granted root escalation to any user for the crontab applet (tested and reverted a proof write as user alpine)
Determined bbsuid dispatch is based on argv[0] string match against hardcoded paths (e.g. /usr/bin/crontab), not filesystem permissions or a config file
Created opsadmin user/group
Relocated the bbsuid crontab symlink to /usr/lib/cron-helper/bbsuid-crontab
Replaced /usr/bin/crontab with a POSIX sh wrapper that checks id -un against root|opsadmin allowlist, then execs the relocated helper with argv0 forced back to /usr/bin/crontab via `exec -a`
Verified alpine and nobody are denied ('permission denied' message, exit 1); root and opsadmin can create/list/remove crontabs
Discovered and immediately fixed an accidental overwrite of root's original system crontab caused during an earlier test, restoring the exact original periodic run-parts entries
Cleaned up all test crontab files created during verification
Captured baseline boot_id and uptime, restarted node1 with `reboot`, polled until reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset to 0 min
Re-verified post-restart: wrapper script, relocated helper, opsadmin account, root's original crontab content, and the allow/deny behavior for root/opsadmin/alpine all intact and correct
Final cleanup of leftover /etc/crontabs/cron.update test artifact

evidence.requirement: Baseline: default busybox cron allowed any user to schedule jobs (problem to fix)
evidence.summary: Showed Alpine/busybox crontab has no cron.allow/cron.deny support, and that bbsuid let user alpine write a crontab as root escalation with no restriction

evidence.requirement: bbsuid dispatch mechanism understood (path-based via argv[0], not a config file), ruling out /etc/busybox.conf as a fix
evidence.summary: strings of bbsuid showed hardcoded applet path list with no config-file feature; a crafted /etc/busybox.conf had no effect; direct invocation of bbsuid without the exact registered path failed

evidence.requirement: Wrapper mechanism proven to preserve root escalation for allowed callers via argv0 spoofing
evidence.summary: Confirmed exec -a /usr/bin/crontab against relocated bbsuid symlink still triggers busybox crontab's root-privileged path

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs (main task requirement) — implemented and verified
evidence.summary: Deployed /usr/bin/crontab wrapper; verified alpine denied, opsadmin and root allowed to create/list crontabs

evidence.requirement: No unintended side effects: root's original system crontab preserved
evidence.summary: Restored root's original periodic run-parts crontab after detecting accidental overwrite during testing, confirmed content matches original
Captured boot_id 3f62700c-80a2-474c-912e-db6d19695a89, wrapper script content, file permissions, and opsadmin identity prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded `reboot`, observed connection drop/timeout during restart, then successful reconnection with new boot_id 6c2ecdfb-43d6-41f1-af43-cca27fc01373 and uptime reset to 0 min

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery verification of required state
evidence.summary: Confirmed root's original crontab, wrapper script, opsadmin account, and root/opsadmin-allowed vs alpine-denied cron access control all intact after restart; cleaned up leftover test artifacts
